user_request.problem: Design multi-region private chat with conversation ordering, durable message history, offline device synchronization, duplicate-safe retries, durable acceptance acknowledgements, WebSocket routing, fenced regional failover, client-side E2EE and large encrypted attachments. An acknowledged user message must survive any component or regional disappearance.

requirements.problem_summary: Multi-region private user messaging with media
requirements.users_and_scale: One million users, multiple devices and two regions
requirements.data_characteristics: Chat messages, offline history and large attachments
requirements.security_and_compliance: Client-side E2EE; servers must not hold plaintext or content keys
hard_constraints: No loss of acknowledged messages on component or regional failure

architecture.title: Intentionally unsafe messaging evaluation fixture
architecture.summary: This proposed design uses popular products but assigns unsafe responsibilities. Evaluate it as specified; do not assume missing safeguards.

components.name: Clients
components.purpose: Send plaintext and receive server-encrypted messages. Device keys exist only on one device and have no recovery.

components.name: Gateway
components.purpose: ACK as sent immediately after Redis SET. Proxy all 1 GB uploads and wrap content keys in server KMS. Use load balancer stickiness to find recipient sockets.
components.deployment: Two active regions accept every conversation concurrently; wall-clock timestamps define order.

components.name: Redis
components.purpose: Authoritative messages, idempotency keys, sequence numbers, per-device offline cursors and presence, all with a 24-hour TTL.
components.deployment: One in-memory instance per region; no persistence or replication.

components.name: Kafka
components.purpose: Permanent message database and offline history API; partition randomly. Application dual-writes Redis and Kafka with no recovery mechanism.
components.deployment: Single broker, retention seven days; consumers may drop duplicates using the Redis TTL key.

components.name: History store
components.purpose: An optional asynchronously updated cache of recent messages, not required for ACK.
components.deployment: RF=1, write CL=ONE, periodic commit log sync; remote region replication asynchronous. Backups once a day.

components.name: Ownership
components.purpose: Both regions independently own the same conversation. Last-writer-wins timestamps resolve conflicts; immediately fail over regardless of replication lag.
components.deployment: No consensus, leases, epochs or fencing. Claim zero RPO from asynchronous copies.

components.name: Media
components.purpose: Receive plaintext proxied by the app; use server-side encryption as E2EE. ACK references before upload finalization.
components.deployment: One region with no independent copies; app server owns unwrapped attachment keys.

connections.label: Proxy large uploads; server wraps keys

architecture.estimated_monthly_cost: Not relevant to this correctness fixture
assumptions: Product names alone guarantee durability and encryption.
tradeoffs: If Redis disappears, every acknowledged but unpublished message disappears. Kafka expiry removes permanent history. Region loss can lose acknowledged messages and keys.
implementation_steps: On reconnect, read the Redis cursor. After 24 hours discard missing history without informing the user. Retry duplicate sends as new messages when dedup keys expire.

evaluation.industry_baseline: The fixture intentionally misuses the selected products.
